html:
October 24, 2026

Lula defeats Flavio Bolsonaro to win Brazilian presidency

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won re-election in a runoff against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, according to Brazil's electoral authority. The result gives Lula a fourth non-consecutive term and extends the presidency he resumed in 2023 after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. The outcome was not widely predicted after the first round of voting. Flavio Bolsonaro's father is currently imprisoned in Brazil.

Serbian student-led movement unseats Vucic's ruling party in snap election

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Serbian Prime Minister Aleksandar Vucic announced that his majority party lost parliamentary elections to candidates backed by the country's student-led protest movement. Vucic, in power for more than a decade, had called the snap election in an attempt to consolidate his position. The student-backed list is set to hold a majority in parliament, with the ruling party reduced to roughly 104 to 105 seats.

Obama attacks Trump and Hegseth over conduct of Iran war

tags: politics, war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Former President Barack Obama criticised the administration's handling of the war with Iran, saying the nuclear deal he negotiated had prevented Iran from obtaining weapons without military action. He said that seven months after the war began, allies and bases have been attacked, Americans have been killed and hundreds wounded, missile stocks have been depleted, and Iran holds effective veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil, diesel and consumer prices. He also mocked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's focus on troops' jaw lines, testosterone levels and live-streamed executions.

Executives quit $25 billion Alaska gas venture over claims of hidden Russian control

tags: politics, energy, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Investigations by the Financial Times and New York Times reported that a sanctioned Russian energy company secretly funded an American firm pitching an Alaska gas project that was discussed in Ukraine peace talks. Vladimir Putin raised the project with Trump envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, with no direct indication they knew of the Russian ties. The Russian involvement was concealed through a UAE-linked intermediary, and American executives have resigned over the connection. The White House was reportedly warned about the Russian financing and urged to investigate.

Book alleges Kushner accessed billions in secret Gulf-funded accounts

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

A new book by journalist Matthew Cole, excerpted in Vanity Fair, alleges that Jared Kushner accessed more than $2 billion in secret accounts funded by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates to influence U.S. foreign policy. Cole writes that Dutch intelligence agents hacked Kushner's iPhone and observed him accessing a Dubai bank account holding hundreds of millions of dollars originating from Azerbaijan, with transfers to individuals including a warlord, a mercenary and a former hitman. Kushner denied the allegations, calling them completely insane and never substantiated with documents, and his attorney denied the account existed and threatened legal action.

Trump administration exempts 202 polluting facilities from Clean Air Act rules

tags: climate, health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

An investigation found that the administration has exempted 202 facilities across 39 states and Puerto Rico from Clean Air Act regulations that were due to take effect. The facilities include chemical manufacturers, copper smelters, sterilizers, steel-related plants and coal-burning power plants, among the country's worst industrial polluters. An estimated 3.3 million people live within three miles of at least one exempted facility, with the heaviest concentrations in the South and East.

Musk says he cut off Starlink access used by Ukraine

tags: war, tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Elon Musk stated publicly that Starlink had never permitted the use of its service for offensive drone strikes and that a loophole allowing such use was closed last week, saying Ukraine's military had violated the terms of service. He had initially attributed the decision to the White House. Ukrainian civilians died following the cutoff. Kirill Dmitriev, an envoy for Vladimir Putin, subsequently praised Musk as a peacemaker.

Musk's record midterm spending draws scrutiny over his federal contracts

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich

Federal filings show Elon Musk has put roughly $446 million of his own money into the 2026 midterms, the largest sum from any single donor in modern American history, with other reporting citing figures above $470 million. His companies have collected at least $38 billion in taxpayer money over two decades through contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits. Much of the spending has funded online ads attacking Democratic Senate candidates over transgender issues, some of which fact checkers found misrepresent voting records. Musk is reported to be concerned that a Democratic win would expose SpaceX, Starlink, USAID contracts and DOGE to congressional subpoenas.

Republicans warn bottom is falling out nine days before midterms

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican operatives privately described the party's position as collapsing with nine days remaining before the midterm elections, with some saying the race is effectively over. At a Georgia rally, the president said of high gas prices that the country is making money like never before and that he did not care if people were suffering at the pump. Operatives also pointed to his hoarse delivery and a closing message that included remarks about Nicki Minaj's appearance.

White House aides brace for firings if Republicans lose Congress

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

White House officials are anticipating an internal purge of staff, including firings and reassignments, if Republicans lose at least one chamber of Congress, according to CNN and other reporting. Aides describe growing jockeying for position and a view that the president is becoming a lame duck with ten days until election day. A Democratic takeover of the House would stall the administration's legislative agenda.

Trump weighs pre-emptive pardons for junior White House staff

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

According to reporting from the Washington Sun, the president is considering mass pardons for junior staffers in the White House and executive branch. A pardon removes Fifth Amendment protection against self-incrimination for the pardoned offences, meaning recipients could be compelled to testify. Pre-emptive pardons would also signal a belief that the staffers may have participated in criminal conduct.

Trump used golf course conservation easement for $825 million tax write-off

tags: politics, legal, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Forbes reported that the president took in roughly $1.4 billion from crypto in 2025 and more than $200 million from real estate, facing a projected tax bill above $500 million. His company donated development rights at his Jupiter, Florida golf course to a land trust on the argument that the course is a natural habitat worth protecting, while continuing to operate the club, producing a write-off of $825 million. The same structure has been used five times since 2005, and he sued the IRS a month after the Jupiter transaction. An audit agreement struck with his former personal criminal defence attorney, now the Attorney General, limits IRS action on the matter.

Pentagon launches Operation Fortress to make bases self-sufficient for 90 days

tags: defence, war
sources: @aaronparnas

The Pentagon has begun a programme to prepare U.S. military bases to operate for at least 90 days without outside support, according to Fox News. The initiative, named Operation Fortress, is designed for scenarios in which a major war cripples power grids, disrupts supply chains and threatens critical infrastructure. The aim is to remove bases' dependence on standard civilian infrastructure. The plans are described as long-term contingency planning rather than a response to any immediate conflict.

Russia and Ukraine agree Oleshky ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

The White House announced a temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, beginning October 29, negotiated with the involvement of First Lady Melania Trump. Both countries agreed to halt military operations to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations, with teams from both nations visiting residents and arranging transport to Ukraine or Russia. Oleshky's population has fallen from 24,000 before the 2022 invasion to between 1,700 and 2,000, including about 50 children, and residents face shortages of food, medicine and clean water.

Fannie Mae forecasts mortgage rates near 7.5% through 2027 as housing market stalls

tags: markets, economy
sources: @ericmoutsos

Fannie Mae revised its forecast to project mortgage rates of about 7.5% through the end of 2027, up from a previous estimate of around 6.7% for next year, and said rates will not fall until 2028. Home builder sentiment dropped to 29, the lowest reading since June 2012, with 43% of builders cutting prices last month and 65% offering incentives. Existing home sales have sat at 30-year lows for four straight years, and there are 63% more sellers than buyers, the widest gap recorded. Lee County, Florida, has over 24,000 homes listed, an all-time high, and the state has more than two million vacant homes.

Global assessment finds 96% of shallow coral reefs critically endangered

tags: climate, environment
sources: @groundnews

An assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature found that 96% of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems are critically endangered and could collapse by 2075 because of rising ocean temperatures and marine heat waves. The study examined reefs across 127 tropical and subtropical regions, including the Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle and the Red Sea, which together support a quarter of marine species and underpin food supplies, tourism and coastal protection. Pollution and overfishing also contribute to the decline. Scientists said cutting greenhouse gas emissions, protecting marine habitats and restoring damaged reefs could improve survival prospects.

Utah bird flu outbreak on mink farm went unchecked for two months

tags: health, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

An outbreak of bird flu that began in August at a mink farm about an hour south of Salt Lake City is the first at a mink farm in the country, and the farm expected to lose about 80% of its animals. ProPublica reported the virus spread for more than two months without the animals being culled, unlike the immediate response adopted in other countries, and Utah stopped checking on farm workers after agriculture officials said farmers found it annoying. The state veterinarian said practices would change if people started actively dying. The USDA says it has no programme or funding for bird flu in mink and that Congress would have to create one, while the Farm Bill heading to the Senate would allow taxpayer money to flow to the fur industry. The CDC says public risk remains low and there is no sign of easy person-to-person transmission.

New York archdiocese to pay more than $800 million to settle 1,300 abuse claims

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

The Archdiocese of New York has reached an $800 million settlement with approximately 1,300 people who accused Catholic clergy of sexual abuse, the second-largest such settlement involving a U.S. Catholic archdiocese. Archbishop Ronald Hicks confirmed the agreement, which awaits signatures expected in November and would end more than seven years of litigation across an archdiocese serving 2.5 million Catholics. It follows a 2024 Los Angeles settlement of $880 million with 1,000 survivors. New York's 2019 Child Victims Act allowed many survivors to bring previously time-barred claims.

Documentary alleges late Senator Lindsey Graham paid male escorts, including a minor

tags: politics, media
sources: @groundnews

A documentary from The Young Turks and Swamp Watch Studios alleges that the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham paid three male escorts for sex, one of whom says he was 17 at the time. One participant, identified as Kelvin, says Graham paid him $120 for sex in Arizona in 2001. The film, titled "The CLOSETocracy," sets the accounts against Graham's record of opposing LGBTQ+ rights, including same-sex marriage. Graham, who died in July at 71, denied being gay during his lifetime, and the allegations have not been independently verified.

Trump's speech difficulties draw attention at Florida appearance

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

At an appearance in Florida, the president lost the thread of a remark about military equipment, moving from Venezuela to an unfinished phrase and then to the Islamic Republic of Iran while audibly prompting himself to think. The moment added to scrutiny of his verbal performance in recent public appearances.

Trump attacks Obama over rally crowd sizes after Michigan speech

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

At a Michigan rally, former President Barack Obama mocked the president's focus on White House renovations, including a ballroom larger than the White House, a South Lawn helicopter pad and extensive gold decoration. The president said afterwards that Obama's event was empty, though the venue was full, and spent the night posting on Truth Social calling Obama grossly incompetent and accusing him of paying Iran billions. His own Georgia rally received limited network coverage, with Fox News cutting away during the speech.
